name: Yoked rings, 100+10 ms CCW, partner sees light flashes (Persinger 2010)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Persinger, Saroka, Lavallee, Booth, Hunter, Mulligan, Koren, Wu & Gang 2010), yoked circumcerebral rings
summary: The shared field of Persinger et al. 2010: two unrelated people in rooms 15 m apart wear identical eight-coil rings running the same counter-clockwise rotation, 100 ms on the first coil and 10 ms less on each next one (down to 30 ms), while one of them watches dim 5-15 Hz light flashes. Persinger's lab reported power increases in the other partner's right parietal EEG within frequencies matching the distant flashes, only with this 100-ms-based field.
notes: From the abstract (three experiments; unrelated pairs in two rooms; 5, 8, 10 or 15 Hz flashes; right parietal power; fields "based on 100ms, the average duration of normal microstates") and Persinger & Lavallee 2010 section 3.6: two 8-solenoid systems 15 m apart driven by one computer; the time on each of the 8 successive solenoids fell from 100 ms to 90 ms and so on to 30 ms over the right prefrontal region (the lab's "100+10", one turn 520 ms); flashes of about 1 lux for 30 s, 4-15 Hz, strongest at 8-10 Hz; QEEG taken 20 s before and 20 s during each flash train. The sources give no exposure length, waveform file or point duration: the rotated "complex frequency-modulated" pattern is taken to be the Thomas pattern and plays the exact 849-point patent table at 1 ms per point, back to back, the point duration of the lab's later shared-field work (Dotta & Persinger 2012, whose file had 859 points); the 6 min and the flash timing in "setting" (one train per frequency, rising) are this project's choice. Coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal, counter-clockwise from above (Persinger & Lavallee 2010): Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2 lie within 5 degrees of that 45-degree ring (the mapping Fp1, F7, T7, P7, Oz, P8, T8, Fp2 would leave only three coils on the right). Both helmets must run this program and start together; the lab drove both rings from one computer, so two helmets started by hand are offset by the time between the two presses. The light source is not part of the helmet. Source caution: photic stimulation at 5-15 Hz can trigger seizures in susceptible people, a risk independent of the magnetic field. The lab's interpretation (the two brains sharing "the same space") is not supported by its measurements, which are EEG power changes in small samples; single-lab, never independently replicated. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Do not use results for decisions about real people. Nobody with epilepsy, a seizure history or photosensitivity should take part in either role.
setting: Partner A (light): seated in a closed, quiet room with a helmet on, watching a diffuse white light of about 1 lux. Partner B (measured): another room about 15 m away, second helmet running this program, EEG recorded (the outcome; the lab looked at the right parietal region). Flash trains at 5, 8, 10 and 15 Hz, 30 s each, starting at 2:00, 3:00, 4:00 and 5:00 on the program clock; take EEG for the 20 s before and the first 20 s of each train. A third person keeps the flash log away from whoever scores the EEG.
schedule: One session per pair. As a control, a helper runs both helmets on this program or on sham (the same choice for both, unknown to the partners and the scorer) on different days, and the EEG is scored blind.
source: Persinger, Saroka, Lavallee, Booth, Hunter, Mulligan, Koren, Wu & Gang 2010, Neurosci Lett 486:231-234 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20887774/ ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, Theoretical and experimental evidence of macroscopic entanglement between human brain activity and photon emissions, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Dotta & Persinger 2012, "Doubling" of local photon emissions when two simultaneous, spatially-separated, chemiluminescent reactions share the same magnetic field configurations, J Biophys Chem 3:72-80 (859- and 230-point patterns at 1 ms; primer/effector order) https://file.scirp.org/Html/17181.html ; Lehman 2016, PhD thesis, Laurentian University ("20-2" = 20, 22 ... 34 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/e7b03302-1b7f-4f4f-acf5-bdf41ee5370f/content ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Booth, Koren & Persinger 2008, Electromagn Biol Med 27:426-436 (counter-clockwise vs clockwise) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19037792/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
